question: What is the primary function of the neck muscles regarding the cervical spine?
explanation: Neck muscles work together to give the cervical spine both active movement and structural support. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h1)

question: Why must the neck musculature be specially adapted compared to lower back muscles?

options.A: Because lower back muscles do not require any blood supply
options.B: Because the cervical vertebrae are fused into a single solid bone
options.C: Because the neck never experiences fatigue or muscle strain
options.D: Because the neck contains delicate vital structures like the trachea and major vessels

explanation: The neck houses critical airways, food passages, and vascular pathways that require muscular protection alongside flexibility. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h1)

question: Where does the sternocleidomastoid muscle insert?
explanation: The sternocleidomastoid anchors from the sternum and clavicle up to the mastoid process of the temporal bone. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h2)

question: A student midwife notices a newborn tilting her head to the left while her chin turns to the right. Which muscle is likely tight or injured?
explanation: Contraction or shortening of one sternocleidomastoid pulls the head to the same side and rotates the chin to the opposite side, a condition known as congenital torticollis. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is one of the respiratory functions of the scalene muscles?

options.A: Elevating the upper ribs during forced breathing
options.D: Pushing air out of the stomach

explanation: By attaching to the first and second ribs, the scalenes help lift the ribcage during deep or labored breathing. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h3)

question: Where are the prevertebral muscles, such as the longus colli, located relative to the spine?

options.A: At the very back of the neck near the skull base
options.B: Directly in front of the vertebral column
options.C: Inside the main airway and esophagus
options.D: Immediately beneath the skin and platysma

explanation: Prevertebral muscles sit deep in the neck, lying anterior to the cervical vertebrae to support posture and neck flexion. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why do the suboccipital muscles have a very high density of muscle spindles?

options.A: To assist in swallowing food and liquids
options.B: For fine proprioceptive control and head positioning
options.C: To generate heavy lifting power for the head
options.D: To pump blood directly into the brain

explanation: High spindle density allows the suboccipital muscles to relay precise position sense and coordinate minute adjustments of the head. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of the suboccipital muscle group?
explanation: The sternocleidomastoid is a large superficial neck muscle, whereas the others form the deep suboccipital triangle at the base of the skull. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which movement describes bending the head backward toward the spine?
explanation: Neck extension moves the posterior aspect of the head closer to the back, utilizing posterior neck muscles. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h5)

question: How do agonist and antagonist muscles coordinate during neck rotation?

options.A: All neck muscles contract at maximum strength simultaneously
options.B: Muscles on both sides pull equally to prevent any movement
options.C: The muscles turning the head contract while opposing muscles relax
options.D: Only one muscle operates while the rest remain completely paralyzed

explanation: Smooth rotation requires reciprocal inhibition, where the prime movers contract and the opposing muscles lengthen and relax. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is a primary clinical sign of torticollis in a patient?

options.A: Complete paralysis of both upper limbs
options.B: Severe swelling of the thyroid gland
options.D: Sustained abnormal head tilting and twisting

explanation: Torticollis involves the involuntary tightening of neck muscles, leading to a twisted or tilted head posture. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h6)

question: A postpartum mother experiences severe neck and shoulder tightness after holding her baby in an awkward feeding position for hours. What is the most appropriate initial non-pharmacological care approach?

options.A: Complete bed rest with neck traction for six weeks
options.B: Immediate surgical release of the cervical vertebrae
options.C: Application of ice packs and restriction of all head movement
options.D: Gentle stretching, heat therapy, and ergonomic feeding advice

explanation: Mild muscular strain responds well to conservative measures like heat, gentle movement, and correcting the posture causing the strain. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T8#BMP111_U3_T8_h6)
